NOTHING was built, flown or measured; no physical test was run (M-070 not_run, G-MATURE closed). Coefficients without a source are ASSUMED.

hypotheses.title: A high-L/D tethered glider flies steep (tan eps ~ L/D_eff), so the line no longer forms a low clothesline - and what that does to the camera view
hypotheses.method: h1_equilibrium.py: moment balance of a straight line with flyer lift/drag/weight + cross-flow line drag + line weight; bisection on eps; trim CL for max L/D and for max eps; grid l 5-30 m, m 80-200 g, (L/D)max 5-10, Va 3-20 m/s, two lines. Cross-checked by the 3D simulator (sim3d.py): fixed-CL runs settle at 73.3 deg (Va 8, l 15) and 78.5 deg (Va 12) vs 73.6/78.5 deg from the static solver. Camera: env.js bodyPx rule replicated; head clearance = distance helmet centre -> line segment (shared headClear >= 1.0 m).

numbers.effectiveLD_note: tan(eps) = 3.4-7.5 for G130 at Va >= 8 m/s i.e. 40-80 % of (L/D)max 9.15; the deficit is weight at low Va and line drag at long l (line drag scales with (Va sin eps)^2, so steep lines carry MORE normal drag).
numbers.lineHeightBehindExit: eps 70-80 deg -> line 4-6 m above the snow 1 m behind a 1.35 m exit (3.8-5.1 m in a carving lean with a 1.05 m exit); at eps 45 deg: 2.35 m (2.05 m carving). Catenary sag <= 0.1 m for T >= 1.5 N.
numbers.cameraOnFlyer_examples: l 10 m: eps 30 -> 402 px, 45 -> 325 px, 55 -> 264 px, 75 -> 122 px; l 5 m: eps 65 -> 371 px, 75 -> 237 px (upright rider); a 40 deg carving lean costs another 10-20 %.
numbers.headClearance: Pack-top exit: 0.27-0.35 m for every eps/azimuth (the helmet is 0.35 m from the exit itself). Seat exit 0.41-0.74 m, belt exit 0.53-0.85 m, worse when steeper. Only an exit >= ~0.95 m behind the helmet (0.8 m rear boom) gives >= 1.0 m.

hypotheses.verdict: SUPPORTED for the clothesline, REFUTED as a free lunch for the camera and head clearance
hypotheses.finding: A 9:1 glider at Va >= 8 m/s settles at eps 73-82 deg (tan eps 3.4-7.5): the line rises 4-6 m within 1 m behind the rider, so the kite2/towglider clothesline (0.7-0.8 m above the snow) disappears. But (a) a camera ON the flyer then looks almost straight down: bodyPx >= 300 needs eps <= 65 deg at l 5 m, <= 55 deg at 8 m, <= 45 deg at 10 m, <= 25 deg at 15 m; (b) head clearance is set by the exit, not by eps - a pack-top exit is 0.35 m from the helmet whatever the line angle. The flyer must deliberately fly LOWER than it can (airbrake dCD 0.15-0.65 at Va 8-20 m/s for eps 45-60 deg, at +10-35 % tension) or the camera must leave the flyer (H8).
assumed: rider/helmet geometry (helmet 0.35 m from a pack-top exit)

hypotheses.title: Active reel-in keeps the flyer up when the apparent wind is too low (stops, tailwinds, slow riders)
hypotheses.method: h2_reel_sustain.py: S1 straight reel-in (closed form); S2 circling on a cone round the stopped rider with a tension-held reel (sim3d, 20 s, calm); S3 "yo-yo": tension-controlled winch-climb inbound + glide outbound with fed-forward pay-out (sim3d, 40 s, calm); S4 free circling glide (closed form); S5 dock & relaunch. Battery budget per 45 min = 54 stops (27 laps of the R4 run).

numbers.lineEqualsAltitude: In calm with a fixed exit, height = l sin(eps): every metre of line reeled in while circling is lost height. S2 runs lost 10-21 m of height and used 11-25 m of line in 20 s whatever the tension set-point (1-6 N); more tension only burned more energy (15-260 J).

hypotheses.verdict: CONDITIONAL - straight reel-in REFUTED; circling + reel REFUTED; yo-yo pumping SUPPORTED in simulation but costly and unfilmable
hypotheses.finding: Straight reel-in needs line at the stall-margin airspeed: 106 m for a 20 s stop (G130), 46 m (K120) - a 30 m line buys 5.7 s / 13 s. Circling on a tension-held reel cannot hold height in calm (line = altitude). The only reel-only strategy that held height was the yo-yo (winch-climb in, glide out): G130 sustained 40 s with line between ~7 and 28 m at 6.03-17.74 W mean battery power (K120 4.52-12.37 W), i.e. 120-350 J per 20 s stop, 1.8-5 Wh per 45 min = 20-55 g of cells in the PACK (not on the flyer). It fits the battery only if the reel is in the backpack; the flyer swoops 7-28 m round the rider every 5-10 s (no usable footage, head-clearance risk on every inbound leg). Docking and relaunching costs 40-120 J per stop and is the rational stop strategy; the minimum line budget is set by the 6-7 m camera station plus ~5 m of gust/heave margin (h3: 0 m with a CL loop) - ~12-15 m, or >= 28 m if the yo-yo is kept.
assumed: guidance laws (crude; better optimal control would lower energy)

hypotheses.title: "Fly it like a kite": pay out when lift is surplus, reel in when it drops, to regulate tension and position
hypotheses.method: h3_control.py Part A: reduced-order in-plane model (eps, eps_dot, l; inputs reel speed and CL) linearised numerically about the h1 equilibrium -> mode frequency, damping, reel->tension and gust->tension gains, with and without airbrake. Part B: sim3d with Dryden turbulence + rider speed oscillation + heave; controllers 0 locked reel, 1 tension-tracking reel (PI, lag tau 0.02-0.5 s, |a| <= 20 m/s^2, |v| <= 8 m/s), 2 = 1 + eps-rate damping via CL, 3 CL tension loop (servo-rate limited) + slow reel length hold.
hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED for a steep, unbraked glider; CONDITIONAL (supported) when the flyer is braked to eps 30-60 deg and the fast loop is CL/airbrake, the reel slow
hypotheses.finding: The in-plane "tether pendulum" of a fixed-trim 9:1 glider is lightly damped (zeta 0.00-0.2 at Va 8-20 m/s, fn 0.1-0.8 Hz) and UNSTABLE at Va 6 m/s (zeta -0.3 to -0.67: it overshoots over the zenith and falls, also seen in sim3d). At eps ~75-82 deg the reel is a weak tension actuator: dT/d(reel speed) = 0.12-0.3 N per m/s against dT/dVa = 0.7-1.8 N per m/s of gust, so cancelling sigma_u 1.2 m/s would need 4-8 m/s of reel speed. A tension-tracking reel made things worse in time domain (tension sd up to 3.4 N vs 2.6 N locked, eps excursions to 17-48 deg, 10-16 m line wander) for every reel lag 0.02-0.5 s. A CL/airbrake tension loop with the reel only holding length cut tension sd to 0.9-1.3 N (Tmax/Tref 1.24-1.43 at Va 12-16) with eps sd 0.5-1.3 deg and zero line excursion. Braking to eps 30-60 deg raises zeta to 0.35-1.45 and reel authority to 0.45-2.2 N per m/s (dT/dReel approaches dT/dVa at eps 30 deg). Requirements: CL/brake actuator >= 3 CL/s (micro-servo class), pitch-rate/eps-rate damping; reel loop bandwidth ~1-2 Hz for heave and slack take-up, |a| ~5-14 m/s^2, |v| ~1.5-3.4 m/s, mean |P| 3-9 W when it chases tension (avoid), < 1 W when it only holds length. At Va 8 m/s gusts still produce slack/snatch (Tmin 0, Tmax 10-35 N): the low-Va end needs a softer line segment or a slip clutch.
assumed: rider speed oscillation and heave amplitudes
quasi-steady aero (no pitch dynamics of the flyer)

hypotheses.title: The reel as the KE governor; where reel-in to stay airborne conflicts with KE <= 14.9 J
hypotheses.method: h4_ke.py: exact kinematics in the rider frame; identity ground^2 - airspeed^2 = W_t (v_s + Va + 2 v_in cos eps); KE speed cap sqrt(2*14.9/m); h6 riding cases give KE of crosswind manoeuvres; launch_dock stop simulations give KE of fast reel-in at a hockey stop.
hypotheses.verdict: SUPPORTED as a governor by PAYING OUT; REFUTED as "reel in harder"
hypotheses.finding: Any flyer that keeps station follows at the rider's ground speed, so KE = m v_s^2/2 regardless of the reel: m <= 171 g at the R4 maximum 13.2 m/s (207 g at 12 m/s). Reel-in for airspeed in a tailwind adds ground speed by the exact identity ground^2 = airspeed^2 + W_t(v_s + Va + 2 v_in cos eps): with 130 g it never broke the cap in the R4 grid (worst 13 J at 13.2 m/s with 9 m/s tail), with 200 g it broke it in every fast-rider case. Crosswind loops while riding broke it for G130 at 13.2 m/s (16.3 J) and K120 (15.1-17.1 J). The dangerous case is braking: fast reel-in at a hockey stop gave 38-145 J ground-frame KE and passed 0.1-0.16 m from the helmet (K120). A pay-out governor works kinematically (pay out at v_s - v_cap; 1.3 m/s = 13 m per 10 s for 200 g at 13.2 m/s) but eats line; a <= 150 g flyer needs essentially none. Rules: m_flyer <= ~150 g; never reel in faster than KE allows; on a stop brake/deep-stall instead of reeling (H-stop below).
assumed: R4 maximum rider speed 13.2 m/s (kite2 design_notes)

hypotheses.title: Reel on the flyer vs reel in the backpack
hypotheses.method: h5_reel_location.py: flyer reel kit mass (micro gearmotor 9.5 g, spool/level-wind 6 g, 30 m UHMWPE 4.5 g, driver/encoder 2 g = 22 g, ASSUMED class values) + cell for reel energy (from h2/h3), consequences for stall speed, eps (h1 solver), KE at 13.2 m/s; latency/peak-power argument for heave compensation.

heave/tension trim only (0.5 W mean, ASSUMED)
calm-stop yo-yo 40 % of the time (h2 S3 best)

dynamics.exitDisturbance: rider carving: exit speed oscillation ~0.8 m/s at 0.69 Hz, body heave 3 cm at 2 Hz, hockey-stop lean flip moves the exit 8-9 m/s for ~0.4 s (kite2 design_notes rootCause.ke)
dynamics.flyerReelLatency_ms: ~30-60 (pack IMU -> radio -> flyer MCU -> motor) ASSUMED
dynamics.flyerReelPeakPower_W: to cancel a 8 m/s, 0.4 s lean-flip at 5 N needs ~40 W peak and ~20 m/s^2 for a few hundred ms - a 9.5 g gearmotor is ~1-2 W class
dynamics.packReelPeakPower_W: 40 W peak is a 30-50 g outrunner + 1:5 belt: fine in the pack (ASSUMED)

hypotheses.verdict: Backpack reel SUPPORTED; flyer reel REFUTED for this product
hypotheses.finding: A flyer reel adds 22 g of kit plus 4-34 g of cells: 156-186 g flyer, stall +10-20 %, eps at Va 8 m/s down 2-6 deg, KE at 13.2 m/s 13.6-16.2 J (over the cap from ~171 g). A pack reel adds nothing to the flyer and, with the conductive line, removes the flyer cell (122 g, KE 10.6 J, cap speed 15.6 m/s). The disturbance (rider speed oscillation, heave, the 8-9 m/s lean flip at a hockey stop) enters at the exit, so the pack reel can cancel it locally with ~10-20 ms latency and ~40 W peak; a 9.5 g flyer gearmotor is a 1-2 W device behind a radio hop. Line drag is the same either way (same deployed length). The flyer-reel advantage (no moving drum on the body, simple harness breakaway) does not outweigh mass/KE/power.

hypotheses.title: (bold) Crosswind figure-8 / loops (or "dynamic soaring") keep a kite up with zero net reel energy down to apparent wind X
hypotheses.method: h6_crosswind.py: sim3d with the reel locked, vector-field loop and figure-8 guidance on the tether sphere, high-lift trim, airspeed governor (CL reduction + spoiler above 9 m/s), l 10/20 m, two loop centres, W 0-6 m/s, 60 s; KE in the ground frame for riding cases. Physics bound for W = 0: no energy source (stopped rider has no wake; dynamic soaring needs a wind gradient - Sachs 2005).

numbers.loopSpeedsUngoverned: W 4 m/s, l 15 m, no governor: airspeed 24 m/s, tension 31 N for a 130 g glider (Loyd v ~ W L/D cos eps)
numbers.orbitRate_degPerS: line-of-sight rate of the rider from the looping flyer: p50 13-55, p90 20-78 deg/s (shared jitter rule p90 <= 3 deg/s)

hypotheses.verdict: CONDITIONAL - X ~ 2-2.5 m/s (130 g glider) and ~1.5 m/s (120 g low-loading kite); REFUTED at a stop in calm (X > 0 by first principles); loops are a survival mode, not a filming mode
hypotheses.finding: Crosswind loops halve the wind floor of the 9:1 glider (static 4.6 -> loops 2.0-2.5 m/s, pattern- and controller-dependent) and give the low-wing-loading kite 1.5 m/s (static 2.0). Ungoverned loops are violent (24 m/s, 31 N at W 4 m/s), so a speed governor is mandatory; with it, riding cases at Va 3 m/s still reached 14-17 J at 12-13.2 m/s rider speed. The orbiting viewpoint sweeps the rider at typically 13-55 deg/s (p50), up to 78 deg/s (p90), far above the 3 deg/s jitter rule. Calm at a stop: nothing in the simulations sustained at W 0-1 m/s, as physics requires. Circular loops twist the line (one turn per loop) - figure-8 or a swivel is required. Guidance here is crude; an optimised controller could lower X somewhat, never to 0.
assumed: uniform wind (no gradient near the snow)

hypotheses.title: (bold, own) When the tailwind exceeds the rider speed the stable station flips AHEAD of the rider - fly the kite in front and film the face
hypotheses.method: Kinematics of apparent wind (h4) over the R4 wind grid, dead-band classification with X (h6) and the static floor (h1); geometry of the transition.
hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED as a product mode (physically true)
hypotheses.finding: Apparent wind reverses whenever the tailwind component exceeds the rider speed (R4: tail 9 with any rider below 9 m/s, every push-off in tail >= 3 m/s, short turns at 8 m/s in tail 9). The flyer's equilibrium is then downwind = ahead. But the transition passes through |Va| < X (no flight) and over the rider's head, and a line in front of the body is a face/neck hazard. At 12 m/s riding the G130 is "static" in calm/head/cross/tail <= 6 and "loops-only" in tail 9 (Va 3); at 8 m/s tail 6 is loops-only and tail 9 is dead/reversed; at 4 m/s (push-off, moguls) most tail cases are dead. These are wind-gate / dock cases, not flight cases.

hypotheses.title: (bold, own) Put the camera ON THE LINE 5-6 m from the exit (kite-aerial-photography style) and let the flyer fly high and steep
hypotheses.method: h1 geometry: camera clamped on a straight line at s metres from the exit, flyer at l = 20 m; env.js bodyPx rule.
hypotheses.verdict: SUPPORTED (geometry) - CONDITIONAL on eps <= 60-65 deg and a stabilised camera mount
hypotheses.finding: A line-mounted camera at 5-6 m gives bodyPx 369-435 at eps 60 deg, 422-497 at 55 deg, 472-556 at 50 deg, at a 5.4-6.4 m distance and a depression equal to eps. The camera sits ON the line, so its own line runs end-on towards the subject (no clothesline across the frame), it moves only s/l (25-30 %) of the flyer motion (gust and loop motion attenuated), and the flyer can stay at 15-30 m where it is >= 10 m from the head and in cleaner air. The flyer must still be braked to eps <= 60-65 deg (H1/H9), and the camera needs a Picavet/gimbal against line swing. Kite aerial photography already hangs cameras on the line (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kite_aerial_photography).
assumed: straight line between exit and flyer (sag <= 0.1 m at T >= 1.5 N)
camera mass not modelled in the equilibrium

hypotheses.title: (bold, own) "Fly braked": one airbrake setting fixes the camera angle, the pendulum damping and the reel authority at once
hypotheses.method: h1 brake bisection + h3 linearisation of the braked equilibria.
hypotheses.finding: Braking the G130 from eps 75-81 deg down to 45-60 deg raises damping from zeta 0.01-0.16 to 0.13-0.95, raises reel authority 2-6x (0.27-1.3 N per m/s), and puts the camera geometry in the 300-px window, at a tension cost of +11-13 % (60 deg), +36-38 % (45 deg), ~+95 % (30 deg) - still <= 15 N at Va 16 m/s for 45 deg. The "high L/D" requirement therefore becomes "high L/D with a large, fast drag modulation range (dCD 0-0.7)": the L/D is spent on climbing to station at low Va, the brake on holding it at high Va.
assumed: brake as a pure dCD (spoiler/split flap) without CL change

hypotheses.title: Launch from the back at rider speed 3-8 m/s
hypotheses.method: launch_dock.py: closed-form release envelope + sim3d release 0.4 m behind/0.3 m above the exit on a 0.5 m line, CL scheduled so lift <= 3 mg, pay-out-only tension control (T_ref 0.5 N) to 12 m.
hypotheses.finding: The 130 g glider needs Va >= 5.3 m/s to release and ~7 m/s to climb briskly: in calm it cannot launch below ~6 m/s rider speed (Va 4-5 m/s: falls; Va 6: 3.3 s to 3 m and stalls out of the climb; Va 7: 1.3 s to 3 m, 4.9 s to 6 m; Va 8: 0.7/2.9 s; Va 12-16: 0.5/1.3-1.6 s). With a 3 m/s tailwind the rider must exceed ~8.3 m/s. The 120 g low-loading kite launches from Va 4 m/s (1.8 s to 3 m) but pulls 16-83 N on the way up unless depowered. Releasing from the pack top passes 0.47-0.65 m from the helmet in every case - launch must start from a station >= 1 m from the helmet (rear boom or seat holster, as towglider did) to meet headClear. At high Va a full-CL release loops the flyer over and into the snow (first runs, 380 N) - the release CL must be scheduled with airspeed (pitot), exactly like a kite launched in strong wind.

hypotheses.title: Hockey stop and docking: reel in fast, or brake?
hypotheses.method: launch_dock.py: rider 12 -> 0 m/s in 2 s (6 m/s^2) in calm, 0.2 s detection latency; strategies none / brake (spoiler dCD 0.8, CL 0.3, slack take-up only) / fast reel-in 6 m/s / pay-out-and-loiter. Dock snap from line spring (EA 5 kN over 0.5 m).
hypotheses.finding: Doing nothing, the steep flyer keeps its 12 m/s and overflies the stopped rider by 10-20 m (lands ahead). Fast reel-in is the worst option: 38-145 J ground-frame KE and, for the kite, 0.1-0.16 m from the helmet. Deep-stall/airbrake at stop onset with slack-only take-up kept the flyer behind the rider (never ahead), >= 7 m from the helmet, KE <= 9.4 J, landing 7-15 m behind; it is then reeled in along the snow or re-flown if the wind allows. Docking: a rigid stop at 2 m/s closing speed snaps the line to ~70 N; a 26-52 mm compliant dock stroke (or reel slip clutch) keeps it to 5-10 N; relative KE at 2 m/s is 0.26 J. Line elastic energy is small (0.03-1.2 J at 5-20 N), so snap-back is a minor hazard compared with the flyer itself.
assumed: brake dCD 0.8 achievable (split flap / deep-stall trim)

designImplications: 1. Decouple the camera from the flyer's elevation: either clamp the camera on the line 5-6 m from the exit (H8) or brake the flyer to eps 45-60 deg (H9); a camera on a free-flying 9:1 glider at its natural 75-82 deg sees the top of the helmet (bodyPx 120-240 at 5-10 m). The high-L/D wing earns its keep at LOW apparent wind (station-keeping 4.6->~2.5 m/s with loops) - at high Va it must carry a fast, large airbrake (dCD 0-0.7), which is also the primary tension/KE/stop actuator.

2. Put the reel in the backpack and use it slowly: length hold, slack take-up, heave compensation at the exit, retrieve. The fast tension loop belongs to the flyer's CL/airbrake (H3: reel tension-chasing is ineffective at steep eps and degraded every metric). Never reel in to regain airspeed at a stop (H4/H11: 38-145 J); deep-stall/brake instead. Keep the flyer <= ~150 g (KE ceiling 171 g at 13.2 m/s; a flyer reel pushes it to 156-186 g).

3. Treat low apparent wind as a gate, not a flight regime: below ~5.3 m/s (G130) static flight is impossible, below ~2-2.5 m/s nothing reel-free works, and in calm the only reel-only sustain (yo-yo) costs 6-18 W, 18-28 m of line and all usable footage. Stops -> brake, land behind, retrieve/dock (40-120 J), relaunch above ~6-7 m/s rider speed (or use a low-wing-loading wing, which launches at ~4 m/s but needs a 5-10x depower range). Separately, headClear >= 1.0 m is set by where the line leaves the body: a pack-top exit (0.35 m) cannot pass for any line angle - the exit/launch station must sit >= 1 m from the helmet (rear boom ~0.8 m, or a seat/hip holster).
limitations: Point-mass flyer: no pitch/roll dynamics, no aeroelasticity, quasi-steady aero; the in-plane mode damping depends on these and must be re-derived with a 6-DOF model and wind-tunnel/tow data.
Straight line with cross-flow drag (no line waves, no sag dynamics); valid for T >= ~1 N, l <= 30 m.
Uniform wind in the rider frame (no gradient near the snow, no terrain); turbulence longitudinal only.

Guidance/controllers hand-tuned; X, energies and launch times are controller-dependent (upper bounds on what optimal control achieves for X; lower bounds on achievable energy are physics-bound only for W = 0).
Polars ASSUMED for Re ~5e4-1.6e5; low-Re hysteresis/laminar bubbles can cut L/D and CLmax by 20-40 % (Selig, VFS 2026).
No physical test of any kind. Simulation is not physical verification (AGENTS.md).
